candidates.name: Practice guide 77: altering the register by removing land from a title plan
verified_facts: HM Land Registry explains that the red edging on a title plan forms part of the description of the registered estate.
The guide requires the general-boundaries provisions of the Land Registration Act 2002 to be considered when dealing with title-plan extent.
semantic_limits: Red edging or an index polygon must not be treated as a surveyed exact legal boundary unless the relevant determined-boundary evidence exists.

candidates.name: Practice guide 10: official search of the index map
verified_facts: The index map is an Ordnance Survey based index of registered titles and pending first-registration applications.
A search result identifies title numbers affecting the searched land and registration type/tenure.
Plans issued with index-map search results are illustrative only and do not define the extent of an individual title.
HM Land Registry warns that title-plan boundaries show general position, may be distorted by scale, and scaled measurements may not match ground measurements.
semantic_limits: Index-map or illustrative-plan geometry is identity/context evidence only and cannot replace exact INSPIRE polygon containment or legal-boundary evidence.
